claim_text: Maintaining a healthy and safe working environment and enhancing the physical and mental wellbeing of our people.
metric_name: Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate (TRIFR); Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR); Corrective actions completed; Health monitoring assessments
context_text: Maintaining a healthy and safe working environment and enhancing the physical and mental wellbeing of our people.；OUR FY25 HEALTH AND SAFETY PERFORMANCE ZERO fatalities and permanent disabling injuries/illnesses. 99% of corrective actions raised through our hazard reporting process were completed. 900 assessments as part of our comprehensive health monitoring program. Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate (TRIFR) FY25 3.71 FY24 2.96 FY23 2.08. Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) FY25 0.14 FY24 0.14 FY23 0.07.；During FY25, MinRes remained steady in our Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) of 0.14. This reflects a need to continue improving our risk management culture and our safety performance. MinRes’ Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate (TRIFR) was 3.71, an increase from 2.96 in FY24 due to improved injury governance and reporting.
label: Partially Supported
rationale_short: 报告提供了零死亡、99%整改完成率和健康监测等相关数据，但TRIFR由2.96升至3.71，无法充分证明整体“healthy and safe working environment”与“enhancing wellbeing”。
notes: 证据合并自安全章节首页、FY25安全绩效图表和伤害频率说明。
llm_reason: The claim's decisive assertion is that the company is successfully maintaining a safe working environment and enhancing employee physical and mental wellbeing. The evidence provides raw safety rates (TRIFR 3.71, LTIFR 0.14), a corrective action completion rate (99%), and a count of health assessments (900). The evidence lacks baselines, targets, or trend data to verify whether the safety rates constitute a 'safe' environment or if wellbeing is being 'enhanced' rather than merely monitored. The health assessment count substantiates monitoring activity but does not substantiate the outcome assertion of enhanced wellbeing. Consequently, the evidence supports safety and health monitoring processes but does not substantively verify the outcome-based assertions of safety status and wellbeing improvement.
